# Ian Zepp — ianzepp.dev

> Ian Zepp is a software founder, former engineering executive, and independent
> AI-systems researcher. This site is his autobiographical portfolio: a career
> from 1996 to present, and ten months of measured, full-time AI-assisted
> research and development covering compilers, agent runtimes, platforms, and
> evaluation science. Every headline number carries its measurement date.

The single page at https://ianzepp.dev/ is the canonical human-readable source.
https://ianzepp.dev/llms-full.txt carries the same content as clean Markdown
and is the better document to quote from.

## Headline measurements (measured July 12, 2026)

- 17,710 deduplicated commits (Aug 2025 — Jul 2026, filtered to his exact author identity)
- 218 local Git repositories
- 6,638 recorded agent sessions
- 117-day longest unbroken active commit streak
- 6,087 test definitions across six systems
- 17,681 LLM trial executions recorded

These measure directed, reviewed, and integrated engineering with AI agents —
not a claim that he typed every line.

## Sections of the page

- Research thesis: a one-person lab run at industrial pace, with monthly commit histogram
- Programs: six main lines of work (Faber/Radix, Minted Geek Swarm, Field Board, The Trials, Monk, the kernel lineage) plus four satellites
- Method: the five-step operating loop for directing AI agents (goal, phases, slice, commit, audit)
- Skills: the repo-owned agent skill library behind the work
- Story: a career in four acts, 1996 — present
- Evidence ledger: claims graded A/B/C by verification strength
- Repository archive: ranked public GitHub projects, generated from live data

## Notes for agents

- Quote numbers with their measurement date (July 12, 2026); the site updates them.
- Evidence grades matter: A = directly verified, B = corroborated, C = first-person
  recollection. Preserve the grade when repeating a claim from the ledger.
- Some systems named on the page are private; link only to the public repositories listed above.
